display: Angra dos Reis + Ilha Grande (Costa Verde)
tagline: 365 islands, car-free Ilha Grande and UNESCO Paraty — a Croatia-class cruising ground an hour from a 13-million-person metro, with the Rio road slog begging to become a water corridor.
summary: The Costa Verde — Rio state's green coast — is Brazil's most beloved island-hopping cruising ground. The Baía da Ilha Grande around Angra dos Reis holds reputedly 365 islands and 2,000+ beaches, fringed by marinas and the Rio elite's weekend fleet; at its heart sits car-free Ilha Grande, and at the western end UNESCO Paraty. The mobility pattern is pure island-hopping on slow launches and private speedboats, plus a busy mainland-to-island ferry. The marquee longer corridors run east to Rio de Janeiro (~60 nm, today a congested coastal road) and on to Búzios. A foiling-electric layer flies above the bay chop, silent and zero-wake in the Atlantic-forest conservation zones, collapsing the island-hopping transfers and — with Quanta-LR — turning the Rio road slog into a fast clean water corridor.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The entire bay island-hopping network — Angra↔Ilha Grande (~9 nm), ↔offshore islands (~5–12 nm), ↔Mangaratiba (~14 nm) — sits comfortably inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope with marina charging; zero-wake in the conservation zones.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR's 2,000 nm hybrid range covers the longer corridors — Paraty (~28 nm), Rio de Janeiro (~60 nm) and Búzios (~120 nm, refuel-mid-node Rio) — with no charging-infrastructure dependency, turning the Rio road slog into a water corridor.

competitive_landscape: The bay is served today by conventional launches, schooners and private speedboats plus a busy mainland-to-island ferry (Conceição de Jacareí ↔ Abraão). Demand is strong and affluent, but the experience is slow and diesel. There is no foiling incumbent — and the Atlantic-forest marine-conservation zones reward silent zero-wake foiling.
seasonality: Dec–Mar (austral summer) is peak — warm, busy, afternoon thunderstorms; Apr–Oct is drier and calmer, a long shoulder/winter operating window with mild temperatures. Sheltered bay water inside the Baía da Ilha Grande; the Rio/Búzios open-coast corridors see more Atlantic swell. No cyclone exposure.
regulatory_note: The Brazilian Navy (Capitania dos Portos) governs vessel class + crew + cabotage; ANTAQ handles waterway passenger services; ICMBio / the state agency INEA govern the Ilha Grande state park + Atlantic-forest marine zones (anchoring/wake regime — a zero-wake differentiator); the Angra and Paraty municipalities hold marina concessions.
signature_routes: Angra ↔ Ilha Grande / Abraão (car-free island access)
Angra ↔ Rio de Janeiro (flagship hybrid line-haul, ~60 nm)

precedents.why_it_matters: Demonstrates electric foiling as the backbone of inter-island mobility at national scale — the proof that a foiling fleet can be the transport layer, not a novelty.
